question.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, the exact solutions to the equation $2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)+2=0,$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$  are

${x}_{1}=$
 {{field-1}}$,\,{x}_{2}=$ 
{{field-2}}$,\,{x}_{3}=$ 
{{field-3}}$,\,{x}_{4}=$ 
{{field-4}}$,\,{x}_{5}=$ 
{{field-5}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)+2 & =0 \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x) & =-2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(5x) & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & =\pi +2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{\pi +2n\pi }{5} \\ x & =\frac{(2n+1)\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{5}.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{3\pi }{5}.$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\pi .$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{5}.$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\frac{9\pi }{5}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ 

So, in ascending order, the solutions are

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{5},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{3\pi }{5},\,{x}_{3}=\pi ,\,{x}_{4}=\frac{7\pi }{5},\,{x}_{5}=\frac{9\pi }{5}.
$$
